Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tidycrates 0.2.0

  • dig_search() searches the ‘Discogs’ database by a query, by filters or by both, and returns one row per release, master release, artist or label. It needs a token. dig_tally() and dig_plot() can count the results by genre, style, format, label, country, year or decade, and dig_plot() counts “results” instead of “releases” when they include artists or labels.
  • dig_collection() returns the media and sleeve condition of each copy as factors from best to worst, with the same grades as dig_price_suggestions(). The collection fields are read with one more request, and only when a copy has a value in one of them. If that request fails, the conditions are NA and the collection is kept.
  • An HTTP error for one of several IDs now stops with the message from ‘Discogs’, without a purrr error about the index around it.
  • A response body of null gives a row of NA instead of returning NULL without a message.
  • dig_collection_value() keeps the sign of negative values.
  • dig_collection_folders() lists the folders of a collection with their IDs, which dig_collection() takes as folder.
  • dig_collection() returns the folder name of each copy in a folder column. The folders are read with one more request, which is skipped without a token and when the token owner is known to be someone else. Then, or if that request fails, the names are NA and the collection is kept.
  • dig_companies() unnests the labels and other companies of releases.
  • dig_cache_clear() empties the cache.
  • dig_collection(), dig_wantlist(), dig_collection_folders() and dig_collection_value() use the owner of the token when no username is given.
  • Requests are counted over a moving window of 60 seconds. Up to 59 requests with a token, or 24 without, are sent at once, and later ones wait until the window has room. A message says how long each wait or retry takes. Before, a full minute of requests was sent at once and more followed within the same minute, so a long batch could exceed the rate limit of ‘Discogs’.
  • A rate limit that is still exceeded after several tries gives a message and returns NULL, as when the API cannot be reached.
  • dig_search(all = TRUE) stops before fetching more than 100 pages.
  • dig_wantlist() leaves out the notes of the user, as dig_collection() does.
  • Tokens with spaces or line breaks inside, and usernames made only of dots, are rejected.
  • jsonlite is now imported. It was needed to read every response but was only suggested. httr2 1.2.2 and, for plots, ggplot2 3.5.2 are now required.
  • The made-up data of the tests and README agree with each other.

tidycrates 0.1.0

First release.

  • Core request layer with token authentication, a custom user agent, throttling to the ‘Discogs’ rate limit, retries after HTTP 429, pagination and optional caching.
  • dig_release(), dig_master(), dig_artist() and dig_label() read the ‘Discogs’ database. Images and prices are left out.
  • dig_tracklist(), dig_credits(), dig_formats() and dig_identifiers() unnest release data into one row per item.
  • dig_artist_releases(), dig_label_releases() and dig_master_versions() list releases, with all pages on request.
  • dig_collection() and dig_wantlist() list the collection and wantlist of a user. Private ones can be read with the token of their owner, and neither is cached.
  • dig_price_stats(), dig_price_suggestions() and dig_collection_value() read marketplace data. They are never cached, and the last two need a token.
  • dig_tally() counts a collection, a wantlist or the output of the database and list functions by genre, style, format, label, artist, role, country, year, decade or month added. dig_plot() plots the counts with ggplot2 as labelled lollipops, columns or a growth line, with titles, subtitles and alt text.
  • Cached responses are kept for at most six hours, as the API Terms of Use require.
  • Plots carry the caption “Data provided by Discogs.”, which the API Terms of Use require. The help pages and README explain which fields are CC0 and that collections, wantlists, usernames and marketplace data are Restricted Data.
  • The tests and README examples use made-up data instead of data from ‘Discogs’. data-raw/fixtures.R creates it.
  • IDs can also be given as codes copied from ‘Discogs’, such as "[a514141]" or "a514141". A code of the wrong type, such as a master release code given to dig_release(), gives an error that names the right function.
  • Unknown release dates, which ‘Discogs’ gives as "0", are NA.
  • README and pkgdown site in the glacier theme of mcanzi.de.
